instructions:
Each item is an ontology term that a column of sample metadata in a gene
expression study can mean. Write up to 5 aliases for each term: other ways a
researcher would write that same variable as a column header in sample
metadata.

Good aliases:
- common abbreviations and acronyms ("sbp" for systolic blood pressure)
- shorter everyday phrasings ("systolic bp", "visual acuity")
- the plain name of the quantity when the term's label is wordy
  ("intraocular pressure" for "intraocular pressure measurement")

Rules:
- An alias must mean the same variable as the term: not a broader or narrower
  one, and not a related one.
- No values ("male", "high"), units on their own, gene or tool names, or
  dataset-specific codes.
- No alias that only rewords the label trivially (plural, case,
  punctuation). Those are matched already.
- Fewer is better than wrong. If a term has no natural alias, return an empty
  list.

Examples:
- systolic blood pressure -> ["sbp", "systolic bp", "systolic pressure"]
- intraocular pressure measurement -> ["intraocular pressure", "iop"]
- visual acuity measurement -> ["visual acuity", "va"]

items.definition: Conceptual functions or thinking in all its forms.

items.label: body weights and measures
items.definition: Measurements of the height, weight, length, area, etc., of the human and animal body or its parts.

items.label: episodic memory
items.definition: Type of declarative memory, consisting of personal memory in contrast to general knowledge.

items.label: short-term memory
items.definition: Remembrance of information for a few seconds to hours.

items.label: body weight
items.definition: The mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual. It is expressed by units of pounds or kilograms.

items.label: body mass index

items.label: neuroimaging measurement
items.definition: Non-invasive methods of visualizing and measuring the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM, especially the brain, by various imaging modalities e.g. CT scan

items.label: hematocrit
items.definition: The volume of packed RED BLOOD CELLS in a blood specimen. The volume is measured by centrifugation in a tube with graduated markings, or with automated blood cell counters. It is an indicator of erythrocyte status in disease. For example, ANEMIA shows a low value; POLYCYTHEMIA, a high value.

items.label: mortality
items.definition: Quantification of the number of deaths in a population.

items.label: electroencephalogram measurement
items.definition: Am electroencephalogram measurement measures the wave-like oscillations of electric potential between parts of the brain.

items.label: event-related brain oscillation
items.definition: The measurement of wave-like oscillations of electric potential between parts of the brain recorded by EEG that are the result of a specific stimulus

items.label: psychomotor performance
items.definition: The coordination of a sensory or ideational (cognitive) process and a motor activity.

items.label: personality trait
items.definition: The characteristics in behavior that a certain person has.

items.label: social desirability
items.definition: A personality trait rendering the individual acceptable in social or interpersonal relations. It is related to social acceptance, social approval, popularity, social status, leadership qualities, or any quality making him a socially desirable companion.

items.label: unit of flow rate
items.definition: A unit which measures substance that passes through or onto a given area per unit of time.

items.label: initial time point
items.definition: The first time point measured at the start of some process.

items.label: karyotype
items.definition: A karyotype is the number and appearance of chromosomes in the nucleus of a eukaryotic cell.

items.label: inbred
items.definition: Property of an organism which indicates that the organism's parents were genetically related (potentially for several generations). Inbreeding results in closer homozygosity.

items.label: outbred
items.definition: Propety of an organism which indicates that the organism's parents are not closely related (e.g. family members).

items.label: environmental history
items.definition: Information concerning the envinonrment a material entity has been exposed to, such as an organism from a lake.

items.label: cohort
items.definition: A cohort is a collection of material entities grouped together based on some common property of interest, such as age or disease stage.

items.label: peer review quality control role
items.definition: The role of a material which has been reviewed under peer review for quality control purposes.

items.label: carcinogen role
items.definition: Any chemical, biological or physical agents that increase the risk of neoplasms in humans or animals. items.label: ferritin measurement
items.definition: A ferritin measurement a is measurement of ferritin level  in serum as an indicator of iron metabolism

items.label: soluble transferrin receptor measurement
items.definition: A soluble transferrin receptor measurement  (sTfR) is a measure of the level of the Soluble transferrin receptor protein in blood as a measure of iron metabolism.

items.label: iron biomarker measurement
items.definition: An iron biomarker measurement is a measurement of some molecule e.g. protein or metabolite which is used as a measure of iron metabolism

items.label: insulin measurement
items.definition: An insulin measurement is a measure of insulin typically performed in the diagnosis of patients

items.label: glucose measurement
items.definition: Is any quantification of glucose.

items.label: HOMA-B
items.definition: The HOMA-B measurement employs the homeostatic model assessment (HOMA)  to quantify beta-cell function.
synonyms: homeostasis model assessment B cell function

items.label: insulin sensitivity measurement
items.definition: An insulin sensitivity measurement is a measurement of insulin metabolism, which can be measured in a number of ways, for example using the HOMA model or via a glucose tolerance test.

items.label: HOMA-IR
items.definition: The HOMA-IR measurement employs the homeostatic model assessment (HOMA)  to quantify insulin resistance.

items.label: adiponectin measurement
items.definition: Adiponectin measurement is a measurement of the circulating hormone adiponectin in serum. Adiponectin regulated modulates glucose regulation and fatty acid catabolism. items.label: hematological measurement
items.definition: A measurement quantifying some blood cell, or component.

items.label: monocyte early outgrowth colony forming unit

items.label: spine bone size
items.definition: Spine bone size is a measurement of the dimensions of the spine.

items.label: hemoglobin measurement
items.definition: Hemoglobin measurement is a measure of the quantity of the metallo protein hemoglobin in blood often used in the diagnosis of anaemia.

items.label: HPV seropositivity
items.definition: HPV seropositivity is the result of a measurement of circulating human papilloma virus specific antibodies used in the diagnosis of HPV infection.

items.label: femoral neck bone geometry
items.definition: Femoral neck bone geometry is the quantification of the dimensions of the femoral neck bone of the femur. Femoral neck bone geometry is used in determining risk of hip fracture.

items.label: bone geometry
items.definition: Bone geometry is the measure of the dimensions of some bone. Bone geometry is used as a predictive indicator of fracture risk.

items.label: bone quantitative ultrasound measurement
items.definition: A bone quantitative ultrasound measurement is the output of a an ultrasound process in which bones are assayed using ultrasound and information about bone density, cortical thickness, elasticity and microarchitecture may be returned.

items.label: muscle measurement
items.definition: A muscle mass measurement is the quantification of the mass of a muscle e.g. skeletal muscle for an individual.

items.label: bone fracture related measurement
items.definition: A fracture related measurement is a measure of some bone or muscular entity which collectively are used to determine the risk of bone fracture e.g. bone density, muscle mass etc.

items.label: soluble P-selectin measurement
items.definition:
The measurement of the soluble component of the P-selectin adhesion molecule. Soluble P-selection is associated with adverse cardiovascular events. Alternative terms include:
CD62 antigen-like family member P
Granule membrane protein 140
GMP-140
Leukocyte-endothelial cell adhesion molecule 3
LECAM3

items.label: ICAM-1 measurement
items.definition: A soluble ICAM-1 measurement is the quantification of the ICAM-1 protein. ICAM-1 levels are associated with adverse cardiovascular events.

items.label: adhesion molecule measurement
items.definition: A soluble adhesion molecule measurement is a quantification of the soluble compoment (as opposed to membrane bound) a molecule known to participate in the process of adhesion, levels of which may be implicated in cardiovascular adverse events.

items.label: mean corpuscular hemoglobin
items.definition: The MCH is  the average mass of hemoglobin per red blood cell in a sample of blood and is calculated by dividing the total mass of hemoglobin by the RBC count

items.label: mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration
items.definition: The mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration is a measure of the concentration of hemoglobin in a given volume of packed red blood cell

items.label: lipid measurement
items.definition: A measure of circulating lipid

items.label: urate measurement
items.definition: A urate measurement is the quantification of some urate in body fluid

items.label: serum gamma-glutamyl transferase measurement
items.definition: Serum gamma-glutamyl transferase level measurement is the quantification of gamma-glutamyl transferase in blood. Gamma-glutamyl transferase is used as a marker for liver/bile duct problems and alcohol abuse.

items.label: alkaline phosphatase measurement
items.definition: Alkaline phosphatase measurement is a quantification of alkaline phosphatase in blood. AP is a marker for bone and liver disease.

items.label: creatine kinase measurement
items.definition: A creatine kinase measurement is a quantification of creatine kinase in blood. items.label: total blood protein measurement
items.definition: A total blood protein measurement is a quantification of protein in a blood sample. It is used as a marker for disease and nutrition. It is performed in the liquid portion of blood and typically measures albumin and globulin.

items.label: HbA1c measurement
items.definition: A quantification of glycated A1c hemoglobin in blood used as an index for blood glucose level over several months.

items.label: planned process
items.definition: A processual entity that realizes a plan which is the concretization of a plan specification.

items.label: genomic measurement
items.definition: Is a quantification of some aspect of the genome, e.g. copy number variation at some locus.

items.label: population measurement
items.definition: Is the quantification of some measureable quality of a population e.g. birth rate.

items.label: bilirubin measurement
items.definition: A bilirubin measurement is a quantification of bilirubin typically measured in serum.

items.label: chemerin measurement
items.definition: A chemerin measurement is a quantification of chemerin typically in serum. Chemerin is an adipokine with important regulatory roles in adipogenesis. items.label: total cholesterol measurement
items.definition: A total cholesterol measurement is the quantification of cholesterol in blood, total cholesterol is defined as the sum of HDL, LDL, and VLDL.

items.label: fetal hemoglobin measurement
items.definition: A fetal hemoglobin measurement is the quantification of fetal hemoglobin typically measured in the blood of children for diagnosis of congenital disease.

items.label: homocysteine measurement
items.definition: A homocysteine measurement is the quantification of homocsyteine in blood or urine and is used in the diagnosis of  B12 and/or folate deficiency, and as part of a cardiac risk assessment.

items.label: interleukin 18 measurement
items.definition: An IL-18 measurement is the quantification of IL-18, typically in blood.

items.label: naphthyl-keratin adduct measurement
items.definition: A quantification of the naphthyl-keratin adduct levels. naphthyl-keratin adduct is used as a marker for exposure to the xenobiotic napthalene.

items.label: complete blood cell count
items.definition: A complete blood cell count quantifies specific blood components.

items.label: lymphocyte count
items.definition: A quantification of lymphocytes in blood.

items.label: HIV mother to child transmission
items.definition: The process of transmission of HIV infection from mother to child during pregnancy, birth or breastfeeding.

items.label: genomic data
items.definition: Genomic data is data about the genomes of an organism.

items.label: transcriptomic data
items.definition: Transcriptomic data is data about RNA transcribed by a cell, cells or organism. This includes mRNA, tRNA and cDNA.

items.label: metagenomic data
items.definition: Metagenomic data is data about the genomes of a sample or samples containing mixed material such as from genetic material recovered directly from environmental samples.

items.label: metatranscriptomic data
items.definition: Metatranscriptomic data is data about transcriptomic data from groups of organisms.

items.label: synthetic DNA data
items.definition: Synthetic DNA data is data about DNA that has been artificially created without initial template DNA such as from naturally occuring genomic sequences in an organism.

items.label: viral RNA data
items.definition: Viral RNA data is data about a virus which stores its genetic information in RNA.

items.label: low density lipoprotein cholesterol measurement
items.definition: The measurement of LDL cholesterol in blood used as a risk indicator for heart disease.

items.label: apolipoprotein A 1 measurement
items.definition: Is a quantification of apolipoprotein A 1 in a sample. It is encoded in humans by the APOA1 gene and is the major protein component of high density lipoprotein (HDL) in plasma. Apolipoprotein A 1 relates to lower observational risk of coronary artery disease.

items.label: apolipoprotein B measurement
items.definition: The measurement of ApoB in blood. Apolipoprotein B is a major protein constituent of chylomicrons (apo B-48), LDL (apo B-100) and VLDL (apo B-100). items.definition: is a quantification of Vitamin B6 a water soluble vitamin

items.definition: Is the quantification of IGFBP-3, a member of  the insulin-like growth factor-binding protein (IGFBP) family and encodes a protein with an IGFBP domain and a thyroglobulin type-I domain. Decreased  IIGFBP3 protein levels are used as a biomarker for prostate cancer progression.

items.definition: Is the quantification of Insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), also called somatomedin C. IGF-1 is a hormone similar in molecular structure to insulin. items.label: factor VIII measurement
items.definition: Is a quantification of factor VIII in serum, Factor VIII (FVIII) is an essential blood clotting protein, also known as anti-hemophilic factor (AHF). In humans, Factor VIII is encoded by the F8 gene.[1][2] Defects in this gene results in hemophilia A.

items.label: nevus count
items.definition: A nevus count is the quantification of nevi on the skin.

items.label: protein C measurement
items.definition: Is a quantification of Protein C, also known as autoprothrombin IIA and blood coagulation factor XIV,] is a zymogenic (inactive) protein, the activated form of which plays an important role in regulating blood clotting, inflammation, cell death and maintaining the permeability of blood vessel walls

items.label: leptin receptor measurement

items.label: protein S measurement
items.definition: is a quantification of protein S, a vitamin K-dependent plasma glycoprotein synthesized in the endothelium involved in anticoagulation and used in the diagnosis of thrombosis.

items.label: white matter integrity
items.definition: White matter integrity is a measure of brain white matter using brain imaging and quantification techniques. White matter integrity is used as a measure of CNS function.

items.label: processed genotype data file
items.definition: A processed genotype data file is a data file which stores information about genotypeswhich has been processed by some form of analysis method, for example normalization or noise reduction.

items.label: biomolecular annotation design
items.definition: Biomolecular annotation study design types are those which are designed to investigate functions, processes, locations and identity at the molecular level e.g. genotyping.

items.label: biological variation design
items.definition: A biological variation study design type investigates differences caused by intrinsic characteristics of an organism(s) or biological system; epidemiological reasons (history of biosources); manipulation, treatment or modification of an organism(s).

items.label: methodological variation design
items.definition: A methodological variation study design type investigates differences caused by application of protocols, hardware, software and bioassay relationships.
